threads.body: [General] Connector/J percent-decodes key/value properties, but this rewrite retains encoded host values. For example, `jdbc:mysql://(host=mdb%2ehost,port=33)/db` now reports `server.address=mdb%2ehost` although the driver connects to `mdb.host`; `parseMariaAddress` does not decode it later. Decode the recognized properties before validation and rewriting, while rejecting decoded delimiters that would make the generated address block unsafe.

replies.body: Fixed in b04e835907 (values) and b963f07b3a (keys): keys and values are percent-decoded as Connector/J does, and the decoded host has to be a valid host name or address, so `(host=mdb.host%29%28port%3d1)` reports nothing.

threads.body: [General] An unmatched `(` in the final entry prevents it from being flushed, so `jdbc:mysql://h1,h2,(host=h3/db` is rewritten to `jdbc:mysql://h1,h2/db`. The downstream parser then reports a partial configured target instead of rejecting the incomplete group. Return the original URL when parentheses remain unbalanced, and add a regression case with two valid hosts before the malformed entry.

replies.body: Fixed in b04e835907: unbalanced parentheses now leave the URL as it is, and `jdbc:mysql://mdb.host,mdb.host2,(host=mdb.host3/mdbdb` is covered.

threads.body: [General] Connector/J trims each host segment, so `jdbc:mysql://(host=h1), (host=h2)/db` is valid. Here the leading space prevents the second entry from being rewritten, and `sanitizeHostList` then rejects the remaining key-value entry, dropping the entire configured target. Trim the candidate before checking its shape and parsing its contents, while retaining the original entry for invalid-input fallbacks.

replies.body: Fixed in b04e835907: entries are trimmed before the shape check, with `(host=mdb.host,port=33), (host=mdb.host2,port=3306)` added as a case.

threads.body: [General] Rewriting `jdbc:mysql://(host=fe80::1%25eth0,port=33)/db` inserts `%eth0` into the authority, causing `GenericUrlParser` to reject the URI and lose the previously parsed `db.namespace=db`. Percent-encoded bracketed IPv6 hosts such as `(host=%5B::1%5D,port=33)` fail similarly when decoded brackets are inserted. Parse the path and query independently of the decoded authority while preserving decoded target extraction, and add regression cases for both IPv6 forms.

replies.body: Fixed in 9b10b1dbbd: brackets are removed from the decoded IPv6 host, and a host with a zone id is left as it is, so the URI still parses and `db.namespace` is kept. Both forms are covered.

threads.body: [General] Connector/J 9.3.0 accepts `jdbc:mysql://(host=mdb.host,port=33,password=(pw))/db`, but this check rejects the balanced parentheses in the password and leaves the URL without a configured target. Allow parentheses in ignored property values while retaining the existing balance check and host/port validation. Add a regression case for this URL.

replies.body: Fixed in 4542c08a0c: parentheses are now allowed in values, while a key or host containing them is still rejected. Added `(host=mdb.host,port=33,password=(pw))` along with the rejected key and host cases.

threads.body: [General] For `jdbc:mysql://user:p(a)ss@h1:1111/db`, this authority-wide parentheses check prevents stripping user info, so host validation rejects the credentials and drops the previously reported configured target `h1:1111`; standard MariaDB URLs are affected too. Distinguish parentheses in ordinary credentials from host-property syntax while preserving rejection of credential-prefixed key-value hosts and safe handling of `@` inside address properties. Add a regression case for ordinary credentials containing parentheses.

replies.body: Fixed in 8e4332e109. Ordinary credentials containing parentheses no longer prevent host extraction for MySQL or MariaDB. Host-property syntax still prevents stripping `@` from address properties, and credential-prefixed key-value hosts remain rejected. Added regression cases to both URL test tables and the host-parser tests.

threads.body: [General] Checking the original authority classifies ordinary credentials such as `(user):example@h1:1111` as host properties, even though the host parser removes the user info. Consequently, `jdbc:mysql://(user):example@h1:1111/db?serverName=h2&portNumber=2222` reports `h1:1111` instead of the ordinary-URL query override `h2:2222`; MariaDB is affected too. Determine precedence from the host syntax after ordinary user-info removal, and add query-override regression cases.

[General] A property block anywhere in a mixed list bypasses the credential-ambiguity checks, even when the later `@` is not in a query parameter. For example, `jdbc:mysql://(host=h1),user:123/a@h2:3306,h3:3306/db` produces `server.address=h1:3306,user:123`, exposing the username and numeric password prefix as an endpoint. The same problem occurs with MariaDB `address=(host=h1)`. Keep the malformed-credential guard for an `@` after a path delimiter, and limit this bypass to verified query-parameter cases; add mixed-list regression coverage.

[General] Lowercasing before percent-decoding makes `%48%31` produce `server.address=H1`, while the equivalent literal `H1` produces `h1`, splitting the same endpoint into different telemetry identities. This affects ordinary hosts and both host-property forms (`parseHostProperties`, lines 206–207). Normalize the decoded host before returning it from this shared method, and add encoded-uppercase cases for all three forms.

[General] Connector/J 9.3.0 accepts `jdbc:mysql://(host=h1,other=[value),(host=h2,port=2222)/db` as two hosts because `[` inside parentheses is an ordinary property-value character. The shared splitter counts that bracket as another nesting level, misses the host separator, and drops the entire configured target. Use MySQL-specific splitting that tracks matching marker pairs and add this URL to the Connector/J oracle cases.

[General] For `jdbc:mysql://2001:db8::1:3307/db`, Connector/J 9.3.0 splits at the last colon and connects to host `2001:db8::1` on port `3307`. This branch instead reports host `2001:db8::1:3307` on default port `3306`, describing a different endpoint. Use the last-colon fallback for ordinary MySQL hosts, retain the MariaDB behavior, and update the unbracketed-host expectations with a Connector/J oracle case for this URL.
